results: 1. Bedside nine-position extraocular muscle examination with documentation of nystagmus, ptosis, and range of motion in all cardinal positions of gaze

adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence

vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Partial fascicular/nuclear oculomotor (CN III) palsy caused by an acute dorsal paramedian midbrain infarct from occlusion of a paramedian perforator artery (branch of the basilar tip / P1 PCA).

Alternatives to consider:
1. Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (atypical, without abducting nystagmus) with adjacent CN III fascicular involvement
2. Top-of-the-basilar embolic stroke with partially established deficit
3. Midbrain demyelination (e.g., multiple sclerosis plaque) mimicking acute infarct on DWI
